provenance: gnomAD genome allele frequencies of the effect allele, as Ensembl's REST variation endpoint lists them (release 116; populations gnomADg:eas and gnomADg:nfe; Ensembl does not name the gnomAD release), for the variants of PGS000072 this page scores. The page's own genotypes are 30 1000 Genomes individuals; this draws population-scale frequencies of the same alleles from a CC0 source (gnomAD's terms also have every user agree not to attempt to reidentify participants). Each point is one variant of the score itself, so this is the same modality from a different cohort, not a different measurement.
split_note: Not rows of any model: one point per variant of the published score, which was not fitted here.
attribution: Genome Aggregation Database (gnomAD) genomes, Broad Institute (https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org/), read through Ensembl release 116's REST variation endpoint. CC0 - no attribution is required; it is given because gnomAD asks for it and a link back. gnomAD's terms bind users not to attempt to re-identify participants.
modifications: Effect-allele frequencies of 177 of the score's 183 scored variants, in gnomAD's East Asian (eas) and non-Finnish European (nfe) groups, keyed by rsID and rounded to 4 significant figures; left out: 6 for which Ensembl lists no gnomAD frequency of the effect allele in one of the two groups; each variant classed by its absolute effect weight, at or above the median or below it.
class_names: weight at or above the median
note: 177 of the 183 variants this page scores, each placed by its effect allele's frequency in gnomAD's East Asian (eas) against its non-Finnish European (nfe) genomes. The diagonal is ancestry-invariant; distance from it is the portability problem in its raw form. The variants are split by absolute effect weight at the median, |log OR| 0.0583 (an odds ratio of 1.06); the published weights are rounded, so ties put 108 of the 177 at or above it. 31 of those 108 differ by at least 0.20 in frequency between the two groups, and 26 of the other 69; a variant's pull on a score across groups is its weight times that gap. 98.1% of the GWAS samples behind PGS000072's weights are of European ancestry (the PGS Catalog's ancestry distribution for the score). This is the mechanism behind the ancestry-strata chart above, not a second finding.
